items.title: PET/CT imaging provides new insights into type 1 diabetes progression
items.text: A novel molecular imaging approach that measures beta-cell mass in the pancreas can offer valuable insights into the progression of type 1 diabetes, according to new research published in the Journal of Nuclear Medicine. The study found that individuals who have had type 1 diabetes for less than seven years have higher total beta-cell mass and function, larger pancreatic volume and lower intrapancreatic fat compared to those who have had the disease for longer. This valuable information, paired with functional tests, has the potential to significantly improve clinical trials of new therapeutic interventions.

items.title: Premature screen use can take away play, movement, and face-to-face interaction from young children
items.text: Nearly half of Hungarian children are exposed to screens daily by the age of 18 months, yet what they need most for their development is play, physical activity, face-to-face interactions and active exploration of their surroundings. Early and intensive use of digital devices may pose risks not only because of the time spent in front of screens, but also because it may take time away from these essential experiences.

items.title: How to prepare youth to respond to firearm injury risk
items.text: Firearm injury is the leading cause of death for adolescents in the United States. Most firearm owners prioritize safety, research shows, but strategies aimed at firearm injury prevention among youth have largely focused on policy change instead of teaching them how to identify injury risk.
